title: latency-backed-reservation-hedger-and-utilization-harvest-agent
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces a latency-aware reservation hedger that proactively adjusts tenant commitments to preserve p99 latency SLOs and a utilization harvest agent that emits sampled, windowed metrics for downstream billing and autoscaler decisions.
body: Context: customers on Dedicated have reported p99 latency regressions during mid-size surges even when overall utilization looked healthy. Root cause: reservation allocation was blind to tail-latency pressure and the autoscaler reacted too late, causing cascading warm-pool exhaustion. This change introduces two cooperating components: 1) LatencyBackedReservationHedger (controller) that watches p50/p90/p99 latency windows and temporarily reduces soft commitments for low-priority tenants and 2) UtilizationHarvestAgent which produces windowed, TTLed utilization fingerprints (per-tenant, per-pool) consumed by the hedger and billing. Goals: prevent latency regressions, reduce recovery churn, and provide stable telemetry for autoscaler decisions. Design highlights: - hedger observes latency histograms (10s/60s/5m windows), converts to an urgency score, and applies soft commitment deltas respecting tenant SLAs and policy guardrails; - harvest agent emits compact HDR sketches and delta snapshots at configurable cadence and supports sampled export to remote telemetry backends; - both components are non-blocking and configuration-driven with safe defaults; - added e2e and unit tests; - backward compatible: feature gated by a config flag and safe by default. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (linear ENG-2891) [x] unit tests for hedger and harvest agent [x] integration test that simulates surge and verifies p99 bound [x] docs/ops updated with tuning guidance [x] feature gate + rollout plan [ ] dark launch to 20% of dedicated clusters (follow-up).
